title: MYP Grade Boundaries: Criteria Levels Explained
summary: MYP grade boundaries explained for students and parents. Learn how four criteria scored 0-8 become a 1-7 subject grade, with examples and clear next steps.
body_markdown:
An MYP report can look like a puzzle: four criterion levels, a total and a subject grade. MYP grade boundaries explain the connection. In most subjects, teachers award an achievement level from 0-8 for each of four criteria, add those levels to a total out of 32, then convert that total into a grade from 1-7.


A criterion level of 6 is therefore different from a final grade of 6. One describes achievement against a particular criterion; the other summarizes performance across the subject. Neither should automatically be treated as a percentage.


### MYP grading at a glance


- Most subjects use four criteria labelled A, B, C and D.
- Each criterion has a maximum achievement level of 8.
- Subject-specific descriptors explain what each level requires.
- Four final criterion levels produce a total out of 32.
- Boundary guidelines convert that total into a subject grade from 1-7.


For the broader assessment framework, see[how MYP students are graded](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-are-ib-myp-students-graded-criteria-explained) .


### What MYP criteria levels mean


The IB Middle Years Programme uses criterion-related assessment. Teachers judge work against descriptions of successful performance rather than ranking students against classmates.


The A-D labels provide a common structure, but their meaning varies by subject. In mathematics, the criteria address knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The[MYP mathematics criteria guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-math-criterion-a-b-c-d-explained-simply) explains these differences.


Descriptors are arranged in achievement bands, commonly 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8. Level 0 applies when work does not reach a standard described by the available descriptors. Teachers select the level that best matches the evidence.


Consequently, level 4 does not simply mean that a student demonstrated half the required knowledge. It describes the quality of the work against a particular standard.


A student and parent ask whether a detective is needed to understand a school report


### MYP grade boundaries for school assessment


The standard boundary guidelines convert criterion totals into final subject grades as follows.


Criterion-level total Final MYP grade Broad interpretation


1-5 1 Very limited achievement


6-9 2 Limited achievement with significant gaps


10-14 3 Acceptable achievement and basic understanding


15-18 4 Good-quality work with understanding of most concepts


19-23 5 Generally high-quality work and secure understanding


24-27 6 High-quality work with extensive understanding


28-32 7 High-quality, frequently innovative and independent work


A total of 23 produces grade 5, while 24 reaches grade 6. Similarly, 27 produces grade 6, while 28 reaches grade 7.


Although 24 out of 32 is mathematically 75%, the assessment meaning comes from criterion judgments and their descriptors. Percentage labels can obscure that distinction.


Schools may also use interim reports or additional reporting requirements. Read the school's assessment policy alongside the[MYP grade boundary system overview](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-grade-boundary-system) to understand how progress is presented locally.


### A worked example: four levels become one grade


Imagine a student receives these final criterion levels:


Criterion Final achievement level


A 6


B 5


C 7


D 6


The calculation is **6 + 5 + 7 + 6 = 24** . That total falls within the 24-27 boundary, producing a final subject grade of 6.


Criterion B offers a useful starting point for improvement. Its descriptors and teacher feedback might reveal difficulty with investigation, justification or evaluation. The next step depends on the subject, rather than on the number alone.


The grade summarizes achievement; the criteria make it actionable. See[how MYP criterion levels combine into a final grade](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-criteria-levels-combined-final-grade) for another breakdown.


### Why teachers do not simply average every task


Teachers determine final criterion levels through professional judgment against descriptors. They consider relevant evidence and decide which level best represents demonstrated performance, often described as a best-fit judgment.


This allows a final judgment to reflect developing achievement without mechanically averaging every earlier task. It does not mean automatically choosing the highest score. Teachers need sufficient evidence and consistent interpretation of the descriptors, supported by standardization.


A productive parent question is: “Which evidence matched this descriptor, and what would demonstrate the next level?” The school's assessment policy should explain how evidence informs final judgments.


### Subject differences and important exceptions


Scientific investigation, literary analysis and mathematical reasoning require different evidence. Students should use their subject and year-specific rubric. The[MYP Individuals and Societies criteria guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-societies-criteria-levels-final-grade) provides a humanities example.


The personal project uses three criteria worth up to 8 levels each, giving a total out of 24. The standard four-criterion calculation therefore does not apply. Read[how the MYP personal project is graded](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-graded-differently-from-subject-grades) for project-specific guidance.


Official MYP eAssessment also follows a separate assessment process. External boundaries may depend on the subject and examination session. Do not automatically apply the internal 32-point table to raw on-screen examination marks. Establish whether a result is an internal grade, an eAssessment prediction or an official IB result.


### Turning the numbers into a practical plan


Write down the four criterion levels, identify the least secure area and compare its descriptors with teacher feedback. Choose one specific action for the next task, such as explaining a method or supporting a conclusion with evidence.


RevisionDojo provides a connected IB resource: Study Notes and Flashcards support understanding, Questionbank practice develops application, and AI Chat and Grading tools help students examine gaps. Across the wider IB journey, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, the Coursework Library and Tutors offer further support.


MYP grade boundaries make the final conversion understandable. The more useful progress begins with the descriptors: knowing what the next level requires gives students something concrete to practise.
